reason: No fixture is evaluated: every file is gated `[typescript]: < 2.9.0` (the rule was deprecated for the compiler's noUnused* checks), and the harness pins TypeScript 4.0.2. The checker question is 'does this declared binding (variable, import, class, function, parameter with check-parameters, destructured element) have any reference other than its own declaration, after shadowing?'. Shared metavariables (M2) and count (M5) can relate a declaration to other occurrences of the same name, but which occurrences refer to it depends on shadowing, which needs real scopes. The port only flags `import {} from "m"`.

evidence.why: `var y = x;` flags y (no later reference) but not x (referenced by y); both are plain `var` declarations and only reference counting separates them (skipped by version gate)
